slices.focus: Denise has minor surgery; Tasha steps into caregiving role, deepening their mutual relationship
slices.summary: When Denise has a minor outpatient procedure, Tasha quietly handles the pharmacy run, drops off soup, and keeps short check-in calls for about a week. The experience shifts their dynamic from Tasha primarily receiving steadiness from Denise to something more mutual — Tasha realizes she can carry some of Denise's weight too. The agent helps her recognize this as 'quiet deepening' rather than role reversal, plan a regular call rhythm (every week or two) to maintain connection outside of crises, and use a simple sentence ('I was glad I could be there for you') when the moment is right. Tasha reflects that her love language is practical: useful small things, not dramatic speeches.
